newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News jumps on U.S. satellite, cable deals.
newsitem.headline: News jumps on U.S. satellite, cable deals.

text.p: Shares in media group News Corp Ltd jumped 35 cents or over four percent to A$6.22 in active Thursday trade after an announcement that News would sell its U.S. satellite interests and buy a U.S. children's TV group.

News and MCI Corp would sell their U.S. satellite interests to Primestar or US$1.1 billion of Primestar non-voting stock and convertible notes giving an economic stake of about 20 percent in a new Primestar group, but no board seats, Primestar said.
Children's cable TV and entertainment group, International Family Entertainment (IFE) Inc, also announced News would pay US$35 a share cash or US$1.9 billion for IFE.
News' ordinary share price rose to its highest level since March 19, while its non-voting preferred stock rose 41 cents to A$5.22, its highest level since March 18.
News' shares have lagged a 9.9 percent rise in the All Ordinaries index since March 18.
Brokers said investors were happy News Corp had not used its non-voting preferred stock, known as DPs, to buy IFE.
They also said News' sale of its U.S. satellite interests had removed the risk that News would be forced to pump yet more money into its U.S. satellite infrastructure.
"The main factor driving the stock is that there's no DP issuance," said HSBC James Capel broker Neil Franklin.
Brokers also said investors had taken the opportunity to push News up after months of underperforming the market.
"It's a brief ray of sunshine between clouds," Franklin said.
"The (News Corp) announcement has removed a number of question marks hanging over the company in terms of its satellite interests," a Melbourne-based dealer said.

Standard and Poor's commented in its statement putting News' BBB rating on credit watch negative that: "This agreement extricates News Corp from the sizable investments and attendant risks in connection with its prior DTH (Direct to Home) business plan."
